To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the orientation and interaction of a biphenyl photosensitive axle and a cap moiety at the ground and the excited states were interrogates by NMR, CD, fluorescence, and UV-vis spectroscopic studies, which led to the construction of highly-defined chiral binding/sensing sites for the photoisomerization reaction of (Z,Z-1,3-cyclodiene) to (Z,E)-cyclodiene.
the photochemical enantiodifferentiating reaction of (Z,Z) 1,3-COD in a chiral binding/sensing cavity of a rotaxane with a photosensitizer axle can provide up to 15% ee of (Z,E) 1, 3-COD.
a biphenyl axle was incorporated into a γ-cyclodextin-cucubit[6]uriel-wheeled [4]-rotaxane through rotaxaneation, and that this rotaxane was used as a host for enantioselective photoisomerization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel chiral supramolecular photosensitizers and their use in the photoisomerization reactions of prochiral dienes.
the development of novel supramolecular photochemical systems, which can be used as chiral photochemical switches.
the development of novel molecular systems that can be used to control and manipulate chemical reactions in a chiroptical manner.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the enantiodifferentiating ability of the rotaxane is a result of the combined effect of the photosensitizer axle, the capping moieties, and the γ-cyclodextin cavity.

the photoisomerization process is not only sensitive to the presence of a photosensitizer in the cavity but also to the nature of the axle and the capping moieties, and that the photochemical process is not a mere consequence of the presence of the axle and/or the capping moities.

the photochirogenesis of the present study is a result of a combination of the following: (i) The enantiodifferentiating ability of the chiral binding/sensing site, (ii) the enantiodifferentiative ability of the excited state of the sensitizer, and (iii) the enantioselective interaction between the sensitizer and the substrate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the photoisomerization process is not only sensitive to the chiral cavity environment, but also to the orientation of the sensitizer axle within the cavity.

the photoisomerization reaction of (Z,Z) 1,3-cyclododecadiene sensitized by the axle of the rotaxane was found to occur in a chiral environment and the enantiodifferentiated product was formed in a highly stereoselective manner.
the combination of chiral binding sites, chiral photosensitizers, and chiral guests can be used to achieve high enantiodifferentiations in the photoisomerizations of achiral substrates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
enantioselective photoisomerizations can be achieved by using the same molecular photosensitizer in different binding environments.
enantiodifferentiating photosensitizers can be readily constructed from commercially available components and used to promote photochemical transformations in the cavity of cyclodextrins.
enantiodifferentiating photoisomerizations are possible with a photosensitizer axle encapsulated inside the cavity of a chiral macrocyclic host.
